notes_list.title: Kathak & Major Gharanas
notes_list.basic_overview: • Kathak: Classical dance tradition associated mainly with North India. • Major Gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh. • Lucknow emphasizes expression and grace, while Jaipur is particularly known for rhythm and footwork.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
👑 Revision Extra Info:
- Lucknow Gharana was strongly patronized by Nawab Wajid Ali Shah.
- Major exponents include Birju Maharaj and Lacchu Maharaj.
- Raigarh Gharana developed under Raja Chakradhar Singh.

notes_list.title: Bharatanatyam
notes_list.basic_overview: • Bharatanatyam: Classical dance tradition originating in Tamil Nadu. • Characterised by precise footwork, hand gestures, facial expression and structured body movements.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
💃 Revision Extra Info:
- Traditionally associated with the temples and cultural traditions of Tamil Nadu.
- Important components include Nritta, Nritya and Natya.

notes_list.title: Kathakali
notes_list.basic_overview: • Kathakali: Classical dance-drama tradition of Kerala. • Known for elaborate costumes, facial makeup, hand gestures and dramatic storytelling.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎭 Revision Extra Info:
- Kathakali traditionally presents stories from Indian epics and related traditions.
- Chutti makeup around the face is an important visual feature.

notes_list.title: Kuchipudi
notes_list.basic_overview: • Kuchipudi: Classical dance tradition associated with Andhra Pradesh. • Combines dance, drama, music, expressive gestures and rhythmic movement.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
💃 Revision Extra Info:
- The tradition takes its name from Kuchipudi village in Andhra Pradesh.
- Siddhendra Yogi is traditionally associated with its development.

notes_list.title: Odissi
notes_list.basic_overview: • Odissi: Classical dance tradition of Odisha. • Known for tribhangi posture, graceful movements and sculptural poses.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🛕 Revision Extra Info:
- Odissi has strong historical connections with temple traditions of Odisha.
- Jayadeva's Gita Govinda has had an important influence on its repertoire.

notes_list.title: Manipuri
notes_list.basic_overview: • Manipuri: Classical dance tradition of Manipur. • Known for graceful movements and strong connections with Vaishnavite traditions and Ras Lila.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌸 Revision Extra Info:
- Ras Lila is a major component of Manipuri dance tradition.
- Movements are generally soft and rounded rather than sharply angular.

notes_list.title: Mohiniyattam
notes_list.basic_overview: • Mohiniyattam: Classical dance tradition of Kerala. • Characterised by graceful, gentle movements and expressive performance.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌿 Revision Extra Info:
- The name is associated with Mohini, the enchanting female form of Vishnu in Hindu mythology.
- Traditionally performed by women.

notes_list.title: Sattriya
notes_list.basic_overview: • Sattriya: Classical dance tradition of Assam. • Developed within the Vaishnavite monastery tradition associated with Srimanta Sankardeva.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🛕 Revision Extra Info:
- Sattras are Vaishnavite monasteries of Assam.
- The dance tradition developed as part of devotional performance practices.

notes_list.title: Bhangra & Giddha
notes_list.basic_overview: • Bhangra: Energetic folk dance associated with Punjab. • Giddha: Traditional women's folk dance of Punjab.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌾 Revision Extra Info:
- Bhangra has strong historical connections with agricultural celebrations.
- Giddha is commonly performed with rhythmic clapping and traditional songs.

notes_list.title: Garba & Dandiya Raas
notes_list.basic_overview: • Garba: Folk dance tradition of Gujarat. • Dandiya Raas: Group dance performed using decorated sticks, strongly associated with Gujarat.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🪔 Revision Extra Info:
- Both are strongly associated with Navratri celebrations.
- Garba traditionally involves circular movement around a central symbolic representation.

notes_list.title: Ghoomar
notes_list.basic_overview: • Ghoomar: Traditional folk dance associated with Rajasthan. • Known for circular movements and colourful traditional costumes.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏜️ Revision Extra Info:
- Ghoomar is traditionally associated with women's community celebrations in Rajasthan.

notes_list.title: Lavani
notes_list.basic_overview: • Lavani: Popular folk performance tradition of Maharashtra. • Combines energetic dance with Marathi musical and poetic performance.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🥁 Revision Extra Info:
- Lavani is commonly performed to the rhythm of the dholki.
- It has been associated with Maharashtra's Tamasha performance tradition.

notes_list.title: Bihu Dance
notes_list.basic_overview: • Bihu: Major folk dance tradition of Assam. • Closely associated with the Bihu festivals and agricultural cycle.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌾 Revision Extra Info:
- Rongali or Bohag Bihu is particularly associated with spring and the agricultural cycle.
- Traditional instruments include the dhol, pepa and gogona.

notes_list.title: Hindustani Classical Music
notes_list.basic_overview: • Hindustani Music: Classical music tradition predominantly associated with northern, central and western India. • Major forms include Dhrupad, Khayal, Thumri and Tappa.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎵 Revision Extra Info:
- Important traditions include several gharanas.
- Instruments commonly associated with Hindustani music include sitar, sarod, tabla, sarangi and bansuri.

notes_list.title: Carnatic Classical Music
notes_list.basic_overview: • Carnatic Music: Classical music tradition of South India. • Strongly associated with compositions based on raga and tala.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎼 Revision Extra Info:
- The Carnatic tradition is closely associated with composers such as Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri, known collectively as the Trinity of Carnatic music.

notes_list.title: Gwalior Gharana
notes_list.basic_overview: • Gwalior Gharana: One of the important traditions of Hindustani vocal music. • Particularly associated with the development of the Khayal style.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎵 Revision Extra Info:
- It is often discussed as one of the foundational Khayal traditions.
- Important associated musicians include Haddu Khan and Hassu Khan.

notes_list.title: Kirana Gharana
notes_list.basic_overview: • Kirana Gharana: Major Hindustani vocal tradition. • Known particularly for emphasis on swara, melody and sustained tonal development.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎶 Revision Extra Info:
- Important exponents include Abdul Karim Khan, Abdul Wahid Khan, Bhimsen Joshi and Gangubai Hangal.

notes_list.title: Patiala Gharana
notes_list.basic_overview: • Patiala Gharana: Hindustani vocal tradition known for rhythmic virtuosity, melodic ornamentation and powerful presentation.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎵 Revision Extra Info:
- Important associated artists include Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

notes_list.title: Agra Gharana
notes_list.basic_overview: • Agra Gharana: Important Hindustani vocal tradition with strong links to Dhrupad and Khayal. • Known for powerful voice production and rhythmic emphasis.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎵 Revision Extra Info:
- Important exponents include Faiyaz Khan and Vilayat Hussain Khan.

notes_list.title: Madhubani Painting
notes_list.basic_overview: • Madhubani: Traditional painting style associated with Bihar. • Characterised by strong line work, symbolic motifs and vibrant colours.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎨 Revision Extra Info:
- Also known as Mithila painting.
- Traditional themes include mythology, nature, religious symbolism and social life.

notes_list.title: Warli Painting
notes_list.basic_overview: • Warli: Tribal painting tradition associated with Maharashtra. • Uses simple geometric forms such as circles, triangles and lines.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎨 Revision Extra Info:
- Traditionally uses a limited visual vocabulary to represent people, animals, farming and community activities.

notes_list.title: Pattachitra
notes_list.basic_overview: • Pattachitra: Traditional painting tradition associated especially with Odisha. • Known for intricate lines, decorative borders and mythological themes.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🛕 Revision Extra Info:
- Jagannath-related themes are prominent in Odisha Pattachitra traditions.

notes_list.title: Indian Handloom Traditions
notes_list.basic_overview: India has diverse handloom traditions including Banarasi silk, Kanchipuram silk, Chanderi, Paithani, Patola and Pochampally textiles.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🧵 Revision Extra Info:
- Different regions developed distinctive weaving techniques, motifs, fibres and dyeing practices.

notes_list.title: Sanchi Stupa
notes_list.basic_overview: • Sanchi: Major Buddhist heritage site in Madhya Pradesh. • Famous for its stupas, gateways and Buddhist architectural remains.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏛️ Revision Extra Info:
- The Great Stupa at Sanchi is associated with the Mauryan period and later additions and expansions.

notes_list.title: Ajanta and Ellora Caves
notes_list.basic_overview: • Ajanta: Famous for Buddhist cave architecture and paintings. • Ellora: Famous for Buddhist, Hindu and Jain cave monuments.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🪨 Revision Extra Info:
- The Kailasa temple at Ellora is a major rock-cut architectural achievement.

notes_list.title: Qutub Minar
notes_list.basic_overview: • Qutub Minar: Historic monument in Delhi. • Construction was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and continued by successors.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏛️ Revision Extra Info:
- The monument is part of the Qutb complex, which contains several significant Indo-Islamic architectural remains.

notes_list.title: Taj Mahal
notes_list.basic_overview: • Taj Mahal: Mughal-era monument in Agra, Uttar Pradesh. • Commissioned by Shah Jahan and built primarily in white marble.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🕌 Revision Extra Info:
- Built in the 17th century as a mausoleum associated with Mumtaz Mahal.
- It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

topics.topic_title: UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India

notes_list.title: UNESCO Heritage Sites
notes_list.basic_overview: India has numerous UNESCO World Heritage Sites representing cultural, natural and mixed heritage.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌍 Revision Extra Info:
- Examples include Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Kaziranga National Park and the Mountain Railways of India.

notes_list.title: Ancient Indian Literature
notes_list.basic_overview: • Ramayana: Traditionally attributed to Valmiki. • Mahabharata: Traditionally attributed to Vyasa. • Arthashastra: Associated with Kautilya.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
📚 Revision Extra Info:
- Kalidasa is associated with works such as Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta and Raghuvamsha.

notes_list.title: Modern Indian Literature
notes_list.basic_overview: Important modern Indian literary works include Gitanjali by Rabindranath Tagore, Godan by Munshi Premchand and Malgudi Days by R. K. Narayan.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
✍️ Revision Extra Info:
- Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
- Premchand wrote extensively in Hindi and Urdu.

notes_list.title: Wings of Fire
notes_list.basic_overview: • Wings of Fire: Autobiographical work associated with A. P. J. Abdul Kalam. • Co-authored with Arun Tiwari.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
📖 Revision Extra Info:
- The book describes Kalam's early life, education, scientific career and experiences in India's space and defence programmes.

notes_list.title: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
notes_list.basic_overview: • The Story of My Experiments with Truth: Autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
📚 Revision Extra Info:
- The work describes Gandhi's life experiences and reflections on truth, ethics and personal development.

notes_list.title: Bharat Ratna
notes_list.basic_overview: • Bharat Ratna: India's highest civilian award. • Awarded for exceptional service or performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavour.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏅 Revision Extra Info:
- Instituted in 1954.
- The award is not restricted to citizens of India.

notes_list.title: Padma Awards
notes_list.basic_overview: • Padma Vibhushan: Exceptional and distinguished service. • Padma Bhushan: Distinguished service of a high order. • Padma Shri: Distinguished contribution in various fields.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏆 Revision Extra Info:
- Padma Awards are announced annually around Republic Day.
- The awards cover fields such as art, social work, public affairs, science, trade, medicine and sports.

notes_list.title: Nobel Prize
notes_list.basic_overview:
• Nobel Prizes are awarded in Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature and Peace.
• The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel is also commonly grouped with the Nobel Prizes.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏅 Revision Extra Info:
- The prizes originate from Alfred Nobel's will.
- Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, while the other Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm.

notes_list.title: Republic Day
notes_list.basic_overview: • Republic Day: 26 January. • Marks the date on which the Constitution of India came into force in 1950.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🇮🇳 Revision Extra Info:
- The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

notes_list.title: Independence Day
notes_list.basic_overview: • Independence Day: 15 August. • Commemorates India's independence from British rule in 1947.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🇮🇳 Revision Extra Info:
- The first Independence Day was observed on 15 August 1947.

notes_list.title: Gandhi Jayanti
notes_list.basic_overview: • Gandhi Jayanti: 2 October. • Marks the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🕊️ Revision Extra Info:
- 2 October is also observed as the International Day of Non-Violence.

notes_list.title: World Environment Day
notes_list.basic_overview: • World Environment Day: 5 June. • Observed to promote environmental awareness and action.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌱 Revision Extra Info:
- Led by the United Nations Environment Programme, the day is observed annually with a specific theme.

notes_list.title: World Health Day
notes_list.basic_overview: • World Health Day: 7 April. • Marks the anniversary of the founding of the World Health Organization.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌍 Revision Extra Info:
- Observed annually by WHO and partners around a selected health-related theme.

notes_list.title: International Women's Day
notes_list.basic_overview: • International Women's Day: 8 March. • Observed internationally to recognise women's social, economic, cultural and political achievements.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌸 Revision Extra Info:
- The day is associated with the global movement for women's rights and equality.

notes_list.title: World Water Day
notes_list.basic_overview: • World Water Day: 22 March. • Focuses on the importance of freshwater and water-related issues.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
💧 Revision Extra Info:
- World Water Day is coordinated by the United Nations and is observed annually with a specific theme.

notes_list.title: Ganga River System
notes_list.basic_overview:
• The Ganga is one of India's major river systems.
• Important tributaries include Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gandak and Kosi.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌊 Revision Extra Info:
- The Ganga basin covers a large part of northern India and supports dense settlement and agriculture.

notes_list.title: Godavari River
notes_list.basic_overview: • Godavari: Major Peninsular river. • Often referred to as the 'Dakshin Ganga' in Indian geographical references.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌊 Revision Extra Info:
- It rises near Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra and flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

notes_list.title: Black Soil
notes_list.basic_overview: • Black Soil: Also called regur soil. • Particularly suitable for cotton cultivation because of its moisture-retaining capacity.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌱 Revision Extra Info:
- Black soils are strongly associated with basaltic regions of the Deccan Plateau.

notes_list.title: Alluvial Soil
notes_list.basic_overview: • Alluvial Soil: Deposited mainly by rivers. • Widespread across the Northern Plains and important for agriculture.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌾 Revision Extra Info:
- Alluvial soils vary in age and composition and include newer and older alluvial deposits.

notes_list.title: Continents
notes_list.basic_overview: • Largest continent: Asia. • Smallest continent: Australia. • Largest ocean: Pacific Ocean.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌍 Revision Extra Info:
- Antarctica is the southernmost continent and is largely covered by ice.

notes_list.title: Major Mountains
notes_list.basic_overview: • Mount Everest: Highest mountain above sea level. • Located in the Himalayas on the Nepal–China border region.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏔️ Revision Extra Info:
- Mount Everest is known as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet.

notes_list.title: Human Body Facts
notes_list.basic_overview: • Largest organ: Skin. • Largest internal organ: Liver. • Normal human chromosome number: 46 in most somatic cells.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🔬 Revision Extra Info:
- Human somatic cells normally contain 23 pairs of chromosomes.
- Red blood cells in humans lack a nucleus when mature.

notes_list.title: Units & Scientific Instruments
notes_list.basic_overview: • Barometer: Atmospheric pressure. • Hygrometer: Humidity. • Anemometer: Wind speed. • Seismograph: Earthquake vibrations.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🧪 Revision Extra Info:
- Thermometer measures temperature.
- Ammeter measures electric current.
- Voltmeter measures potential difference.

notes_list.title: RBI
notes_list.basic_overview: • RBI: Reserve Bank of India. • India's central bank and monetary authority. • Established in 1935 and nationalised in 1949.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏦 Revision Extra Info:
- RBI performs functions related to monetary policy, currency management, banking regulation and financial stability within its statutory framework.

notes_list.title: Repo Rate & Reverse Repo
notes_list.basic_overview: • Repo: Rate associated with RBI lending funds to eligible entities against securities under the monetary-policy framework. • Reverse Repo: Traditionally refers to the rate at which RBI absorbs liquidity from banks.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
💰 Revision Extra Info:
- Monetary policy instruments influence liquidity, credit conditions and interest rates in the financial system.

notes_list.title: GDP
notes_list.basic_overview: • GDP: Gross Domestic Product. • Measures the monetary value of final goods and services produced within a country's geographical territory over a specified period.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
📊 Revision Extra Info:
- GDP can be measured using production, income and expenditure approaches.

notes_list.title: Inflation
notes_list.basic_overview: • Inflation: Sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services over time. • It reduces the purchasing power of money when incomes do not rise proportionately.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
📈 Revision Extra Info:
- Consumer price indices are commonly used to track changes in retail prices.

notes_list.title: Cricket Terminology
notes_list.basic_overview: • Yorker: Delivery pitching near the batter's feet. • Bouncer: Short-pitched delivery that rises sharply. • Googly: Deceptive delivery bowled by a leg-spinner.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏏 Revision Extra Info:
- Cricket is played between two teams, generally with eleven players per side in standard international formats.

notes_list.title: Football Terminology
notes_list.basic_overview: • Offside: A player-position offence defined by the Laws of the Game. • Penalty kick: Awarded for certain direct-free-kick offences committed inside the defending team's penalty area.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
⚽ Revision Extra Info:
- Football is governed internationally by the Laws of the Game maintained through the IFAB framework.

notes_list.title: Olympic Games
notes_list.basic_overview:
• The modern Olympic Games are an international multi-sport event.
• The Olympic movement is governed by the International Olympic Committee.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏅 Revision Extra Info:
- The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

notes_list.title: United Nations
notes_list.basic_overview: • United Nations: International organisation founded in 1945. • Headquarters: New York City.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌍 Revision Extra Info:
- The UN has six principal organs: General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, International Court of Justice, Secretariat and Trusteeship Council.

notes_list.title: UNESCO
notes_list.basic_overview: • UNESCO: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. • Headquarters: Paris, France.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
📚 Revision Extra Info:
- UNESCO works in areas including education, science, culture, communication and information.

notes_list.title: WHO
notes_list.basic_overview: • WHO: World Health Organization. • Headquarters: Geneva, Switzerland.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🏥 Revision Extra Info:
- WHO is the specialised agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health.

notes_list.title: World Bank
notes_list.basic_overview: • World Bank: International financial institution associated with development finance. • Headquarters: Washington, D.C.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
💰 Revision Extra Info:
- The World Bank Group consists of several institutions, including IBRD and IDA.

notes_list.title: IMF
notes_list.basic_overview: • IMF: International Monetary Fund. • Headquarters: Washington, D.C. • Works on international monetary cooperation and financial stability.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
💵 Revision Extra Info:
- The IMF provides policy advice, financial assistance and capacity development to member countries within its mandate.

notes_list.title: Indian Army
notes_list.basic_overview: • Indian Army: Land warfare branch of India's Armed Forces. • Responsible for military operations and defence on land.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🪖 Revision Extra Info:
- The Army is organised into commands and formations for operational and administrative purposes.

notes_list.title: Indian Navy
notes_list.basic_overview: • Indian Navy: Maritime warfare branch of India's Armed Forces. • Responsible for maritime security and naval operations.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
⚓ Revision Extra Info:
- The Navy operates surface ships, submarines, aircraft and other maritime assets.

notes_list.title: Indian Air Force
notes_list.basic_overview: • Indian Air Force: Air warfare branch of India's Armed Forces. • Responsible for air defence and air operations.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
✈️ Revision Extra Info:
- The IAF operates fighter aircraft, transport aircraft, helicopters and other aviation systems.

notes_list.title: Agni Series
notes_list.basic_overview: • Agni: Family of Indian ballistic missile systems developed under India's strategic missile programme.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🚀 Revision Extra Info:
- Different Agni variants have different ranges and configurations.

notes_list.title: BrahMos
notes_list.basic_overview: • BrahMos: Supersonic cruise missile system developed through India-Russia cooperation.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🚀 Revision Extra Info:
- The name BrahMos is derived from the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.

notes_list.title: CPU
notes_list.basic_overview: • CPU: Central Processing Unit. • Performs instruction processing and controls many operations of a computer system.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
💻 Revision Extra Info:
- Major functional components commonly discussed include the control unit, arithmetic and logic unit and registers.

notes_list.title: RAM & ROM
notes_list.basic_overview: • RAM: Volatile memory used for active data and programs. • ROM: Non-volatile memory traditionally associated with persistent instructions or firmware.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🧠 Revision Extra Info:
- RAM loses its stored contents when power is removed in normal systems.
- Modern ROM terminology includes several forms of non-volatile memory.

notes_list.title: Internet
notes_list.basic_overview: • Internet: Global network of interconnected computer networks using standard communication protocols. • Supports services such as the World Wide Web, email and file transfer.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌐 Revision Extra Info:
- The World Wide Web is a service that operates over the Internet and should not be treated as synonymous with the Internet itself.

notes_list.title: HTTP & HTTPS
notes_list.basic_overview: • HTTP: Hypertext Transfer Protocol. • HTTPS: HTTP transmitted over a secure cryptographic connection using TLS.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🔐 Revision Extra Info:
- HTTPS helps protect data in transit against interception and tampering when correctly implemented.

notes_list.title: National Flag
notes_list.basic_overview: • National Flag: Tricolour of saffron, white and green with the Ashoka Chakra in navy blue at the centre. • The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🇮🇳 Revision Extra Info:
- The present design of the national flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947.

notes_list.title: National Emblem
notes_list.basic_overview: • National Emblem: Adaptation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath. • The State Emblem includes the motto 'Satyameva Jayate'.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🦁 Revision Extra Info:
- The Lion Capital was erected by Emperor Ashoka at Sarnath.
- The State Emblem was adopted on 26 January 1950.

notes_list.title: National Anthem
notes_list.basic_overview: • National Anthem: Jana Gana Mana. • Written by Rabindranath Tagore.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🎵 Revision Extra Info:
- Jana Gana Mana was adopted as India's National Anthem by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950.

notes_list.title: National Song
notes_list.basic_overview: • National Song: Vande Mataram. • Written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🇮🇳 Revision Extra Info:
- Vande Mataram appeared in Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel Anandamath.

notes_list.title: National Animal & Bird
notes_list.basic_overview: • National Animal: Bengal Tiger. • National Bird: Indian Peacock.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🐅 Revision Extra Info:
- The Bengal tiger represents India's rich wildlife heritage.
- The Indian peacock is recognised for its distinctive plumage and cultural significance.

notes_list.title: National Flower & Tree
notes_list.basic_overview: • National Flower: Lotus. • National Tree: Banyan.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🌸 Revision Extra Info:
- Lotus has deep cultural and religious significance in India.
- Banyan is notable for its extensive aerial roots and large canopy.

notes_list.title: National Aquatic Animal
notes_list.basic_overview: • National Aquatic Animal: Ganges River Dolphin.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
🐬 Revision Extra Info:
- The Ganges river dolphin is a freshwater cetacean associated with river systems of the Indian subcontinent.
